user.title: Connect to your AVPro Edge matrix
user.description: Enter the address of the matrix. You can paste it straight from your browser.

data_description.host: The matrix's IP address or hostname, for example 192.0.2.10.

reconfigure.title: Change the matrix address
reconfigure.description: Point this entry at a new address. It must still be the same matrix.

data_description.host: The matrix's new IP address or hostname.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach that address. Check that the matrix is powered on and on the same network.
error.not_avpro: Something answered at that address, but it is not an AVPro Edge matrix.
error.unexpected_response: The matrix replied in a way that could not be read. This usually means one of its port names contains an '&', which the matrix's own interface cannot encode. Rename that port from the matrix's web page and try again.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant log for details.

abort.already_configured: This matrix is already set up.
abort.wrong_device: That address belongs to a different matrix. To add it, create a new entry instead.

data_description.transport: Telnet is the default: the matrix pushes changes to Home Assistant within about a third of a second, and it is the only connection that can read output on/off, input power, key lock and the display timeout. It uses the matrix's single control socket, so choose HTTP only if another control system needs that socket.
data_description.polling_profile: How often the matrix is checked for changes made elsewhere, such as from its front panel or another control system.
data_description.allow_writes: Turn this off to make the integration read-only. Useful while you watch it run alongside an existing control system.

options.http: HTTP only — never use the control socket

writes_disabled.message: Changes are disabled for this matrix. Turn on "Allow changes to the matrix" in the integration options.

command_unsupported.message: The matrix does not support that command on its current firmware.

cannot_connect.message: Could not reach the matrix at {host}.

invalid_port_name.message: That port name cannot be used: {reason}.

unknown_entry.message: No AVPro Edge matrix is configured with the id {entry_id}.

entry_not_loaded.message: {title} is not loaded, so it cannot be commanded right now.

send_command_failed.message: The matrix did not accept the command: {error}

telnet_unavailable.title: {name}: the control socket is unavailable
telnet_unavailable.description:
Home Assistant could not open the telnet control port on {name} and is running on the HTTP interface instead.

The matrix is still controllable, but output stream state, input power, key lock and the LCD timeout cannot be read on this wire, so those controls are missing, and changes are polled rather than pushed.

Nothing else should be holding this port. The usual causes are a matrix that is rebooting, a network interruption, or a control session left open by another system. Home Assistant re-checks every minute and reloads by itself once the port is free; this message will disappear on its own when it does.

route_all.name: Route all outputs
route_all.description: Sends every output to one input in a single command, rather than one command per output.

source.name: Input
source.description: The input number every output should be routed to.

send_command.name: Send command
send_command.description: Sends a raw command to the matrix, for anything this integration does not model. Returns the device's reply, which matters because unsupported commands are answered with 'NO SUPPORT' rather than an error. Commands that would change the matrix's network configuration or factory-reset it cannot be reached.

endpoint.name: Endpoint
endpoint.description: Which part of the matrix the command is addressed to.

command.name: Command
command.description: The command code, as the device's own web interface sends it, for example O1I2 to route output 1 to input 2. Letters and digits only.
